extracted.intended_audience: general readers, policymakers, regulatory practitioners, legal and economic researchers
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia encyclopedia entry summarizing the Institute for Policy Integrity’s mission, history, activities, and areas of advocacy (climate, energy, regulatory policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for use of cost-benefit analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy Integrity advocates for the use of cost-benefit analysis in designing regulations on energy and climate issues, consumer protection, and public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institute produces original scholarly research and uses that research to advocate for reform before courts, legislatures, and executive agencies; staff of lawyers and economists author reports, policy briefs, academic articles, and op-eds to support this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Social Cost of Carbon (SCC) to monetize carbon impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy Integrity has consistently supported the use of the Social Cost of Carbon (SCC) to monetize and weigh the impacts of carbon pollution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They frequently collaborate with NGOs to advocate for the proper application of SCC metrics in federal agency regulatory impact analyses and environmental reviews, as well as in state policymaking processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must consider costs when deciding to regulate
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory decisionmaking should take account of costs — courts have required agencies to consider costs (e.g., Michigan v. EPA held that the EPA must consider costs when deciding whether to regulate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy Integrity’s litigation work and amicus briefs emphasize the legal and economic importance of cost consideration in regulatory decisions; this is used both in advocacy and in defending rules in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper consideration of climate impacts and alternative land uses in natural resource leasing
rubrics_metrics.description: When reforming federal natural resource leasing programs, agencies should properly consider climate impacts and alternative uses for public lands, such as recreation, conservation, and renewable energy production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy Integrity participates in Department of the Interior regulatory proceedings to push for such consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage through amicus briefs, public comments, and expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: To influence litigation and rulemaking, Policy Integrity submits amicus briefs, public comments, and expert testimony in court cases and legal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institute’s staff regularly author legal briefs and comments and has filed briefs in major cases (e.g., Utility Air Regulatory Group v. EPA, Michigan v. EPA, EPA v. EME Homer City) to support environmental rules and regulatory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct rigorous research and advocacy on electricity policy (transmission, grid resilience, DERs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy Integrity conducts research and advocacy on electricity policy topics including transmission, grid resilience, and the deployment and compensation of distributed energy resources (DERs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They publish reports, engage in state energy policy proceedings, and advocate before federal agencies such as FERC and the Department of Energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and publicize outcomes of legal challenges to policy changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain resources tracking outcomes of legal challenges to administrative or executive policy changes and make those resources available to the public and press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy Integrity launched a tracker of legal challenges to Trump administration policy changes; the resource has been cited by major news outlets (NYT, WaPo, WSJ), demonstrating the value of documenting litigation outcomes for public and media use.
